title: Governor Braun announces new manufacturer V Tech Conversions in Plymouth, Indiana
text:
Governor Braun announces new manufacturer V Tech Conversions in Plymouth, Indiana
Indiana Governor Mike Braun announced on Aug. 19 the launch of V Tech Conversions, a new manufacturer specializing in mobile workspaces for infrastructure projects, in Plymouth, Indiana. The company is expected to create up to 25 high-wage jobs in Marshall County by the end of 2028.
“Indiana has a long history of excellence in advanced manufacturing, making our state the right pick for V Tech Conversions to start and scale with confidence,” said Governor Braun. “The company’s presence in the South Bend-Elkhart region will contribute to a robust and growing regional economy while creating new, high-wage career opportunities that allow Hoosiers to prosper.”
V Tech Conversions is investing more than $2.5 million over several years to establish its operations at a newly equipped 16,000-square-foot facility on Western Avenue. The company began production in July after acquiring the space in June and has already hired 11 associates with plans to expand its team further. New positions are projected to offer average wages at 165% of the Marshall County average.
President Wayne Nifong and Managing Partner Derek Nick said, “We chose Plymouth because this is home. We believe in building our future right here, surrounded by the people and community that helped shape who we are. Our vision for growth is simple: never sacrifice quality for quantity. We’re committed to building products we’re proud to put our name on, products our customers can depend on, and products that are built to last. For us, success isn’t measured only by how much we grow—it’s measured by the reputation we build, the trust we earn, and the quality we leave behind.”
Indiana Secretary of Commerce Chuck Goodrich said that V Tech Conversions represents an example of a homegrown company investing locally, “Our job in commerce is to help companies like V Tech grow faster so they can create more opportunities for Hoosiers and strengthen Indiana’s economy.”
Indiana supports nearly 600,000 small businesses statewide providing more than 1.2 million jobs and maintains one of the highest concentrations of manufacturing jobs nationally with over 9,000 operations contributing about a quarter of state economic output.
Braun contributed through roles on school boards and as a state representative; grew his own business into a national entity employing thousands; championed over forty bills during his Senate term; won election as U.S. Senator before becoming governor; graduated summa cum laude from Wabash College with an economics degree; earned an MBA from Harvard Business School; has been married for forty-nine years raising four children—all according to, the official website.
